answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is binding each agent to a unique hardware inlet such as a TPM or secure element that continuously signs a thread of activity proofs. The oasis of trust emerges because the attestation is non-clonable: each fake identity requires its own physical device or a costly exploit of the secure hardware. An attacker scaling to hundreds of Sybils faces linear hardware costs plus ongoing management overhead that quickly exceeds typical epoch rewards, while honest agents pay only once.
